title: Preserve representable chord diagram barres and fingerings
scope: Extend chord import/export for authored diagram barres, fingerings and their display-independent identities.
acceptance: Use a chord with two barre ranges, explicit thumb/open fingering and muted/open/fretted strings.
Preserve first fret, string orientation and track/staff definition scope in the independent consumer.
Classify any legacy spelling/omission fields lacking a GPIF destination separately; strict export no longer reports resolved diagram losses.

Add independent evidence using the explicit fingerings from the regression, not only synthesized fingers. Preserve the authored finger meaning; either prove a retaining wire representation or report the narrow Ring/annular consumer loss and refuse unallowed strict export. Cover synthesized third-and-later barres too, because the current fallback finger sequence also selects Annular. Keep exact wire/model preservation and consumer limitations separately classified.
exclusions: Chord display flags are owned by issue 104.
Legacy chord spelling, quality, alterations, and interval omissions remain separate reported losses.
GP3 through GP5 export, rendering, note fingerings, and content deduplication are outside this ticket.

reproduction.instructions: Run the complete TestReviewChordAnnularConsumer reproduction embedded in the latest implementation-audit evidence and linked ticket comment with ALPHATAB_CONFORMANCE=1. The seven-string chord in the reproduction has barres at frets 3 and 5, explicit Index/Annular endpoints, muted/open strings, and a Thumb fingering. Strict export succeeds with zero report entries, while AlphaTab retains barreFrets=[3] instead of [3,5]. The Go writer emits Ring; the pinned reader recognizes Rank but ignores Ring. The current independent two-barre test omits authored fingerings, so synthetic Index/Middle assignments avoid the failing branch.
